query: During Siege of Bharatpur, which Commander-in-Chief of Ireland and Commander-in-Chief of India contributed to the storming of the castle?

pipeline_result.response: The Commander-in-Chief of Ireland and Commander-in-Chief of India contributed to the storming of the castle during the Siege of Bharatpur.
retrieved_context: Stapleton Cotton, 1st Viscount Combermere: Field Marshal Stapleton Cotton, 1st Viscount Combermere {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (14 November 1773 – 21 February 1865), was a British Army officer, diplomat and politician.  As a junior officer he took part in the Flanders Campaign, in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War and in the suppression of Robert Emmet's insurrection in 1803.  He commanded a cavalry brigade in Sir Arthur Wellesley's Army before being given overall command of the cavalry in the latter stages of the Peninsular War.  He went on to be Commander-in-Chief, Ireland and then Commander-in-Chief, India.  In the latter role he stormed Bharatpur—a fort which previously had been deemed impregnable.

Siege of Bharatpur: The Siege of Bharatpore was a siege that took place in the Indian princely state of Bharatpur (now part of Rajasthan) between December 1825 and January 1826.  British troops under Lord Combermere initially surrounded the state's capital until on 18January 1826 its fortress was stormed and captured.
